It was not yet 3 a.m. when the venue at Olympian City was already packed with fans. The atmosphere was electric, with supporters donning jerseys and waving flags and carrying props of the nations they backed, all gathering for the World Cup final held every four years.

In the first half, Spain put Argentina under heavy pressure and enjoyed more possession, while Argentina defended solidly. Argentina mounted occasional counterattacks but did not pose a major threat to Spain before the water break. In the 38th minute, Spain's Oyarzabal fired from the edge of the box but failed to breach the defence. Around the 40th minute, Argentina's Lisandro Martínez picked up the first yellow card of the match.

Right after the start of the second half, Argentina committed a serious blunder in defence, allowing Spain to win the ball high up the pitch, but they still could not find the net. In the 51st minute, a fierce clash broke out on the field as Argentina's Ander Herrera shoved a Spanish player to the ground, sending Spanish fans at the venue into a frenzy, who shouted "Red card!".

In the 59th minute, Spain won a free kick but Argentina cleared the danger, and Spain brought on Ferran Torres and others. In the 62nd minute, Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez suffered a costly fumble. In the 66th minute, Yamal crossed from the byline and Ferran Torres headed the ball on target, only for Martínez to gather it safely. Facing what was so far the closest chance of the match, Spanish fans at the venue could not help but cry out "Aww!" and "So close!", deeply disappointed that Spain failed to score, while also chanting "Well played!" to express their satisfaction with the team's performance.
